decisionsTitle: The templates-changed email is a daily digest
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-15, about 05:45:** «Parcă totuși șabloanele textelor se schimbă prea des, că tot primesc email, de ce?» Six releases in one night each moved a legal template, and §639 sent «Șabloanele textelor legale s-au schimbat» once per change, on the maintenance job's next run: six emails. (On 2026-10-14 he had said «keep that I guess» about a weekly digest; the night changed his mind. Told to decide the open points himself, «YOLO».)

**Decision.** §639's notice becomes a digest, amending it. **At most one email per environment per club day (Europe/Bucharest):** the maintenance job's first run at or after 08:00 club time (`LEGAL_TEMPLATES_DIGEST_HOUR`; 05:00 UTC in summer time, 06:00 UTC in winter time, found on the wall clock with `fromWallTimeInput`, never «plus 24 hours») that finds a text whose template is newer than the text in force and not already announced sends ONE email, naming every text whose template is newer on its one bold line. Nothing is sent when nothing changed; nothing is sent before 08:00, so a night's releases wait for the morning; a change that lands after the day's email waits for the next day's, which names it with the texts still waiting. «At most once in 24 hours» is read as once per club day, so a digest at 08:05 does not push the next one to 08:05.

**The mark.** «The last digest» is `announcedAt` in the `platform_settings` row `legalTemplatesNotice`, where the hourly check and the fingerprint of what was announced already lived: the house keeps its job marks in `platform_settings` (the translation budget, the newsletter's alert lock). It is written in the same transaction as the emails, so it survives a restart. The row's strict shape is unchanged, so **no table, no column, no migration**. Before 08:00 or once the day's email has gone the step reads that one row and nothing else.

**Unchanged.** The recipients (whoever may approve a legal text, §450: every Administrator and Superadministrator with an address, in the language of their staff row, the other language below); the message type, its idempotency key per person per change, its road and its subject; the hourly throttle of the overview read inside the digest's window; `/admin/tasks` with one row per text, which stays the authority; and that the platform drafts and approves nothing. The email's words gain two sentences, in both languages: approve them all in one sitting, and this message comes at most once a day after 08:00 with everything that changed since the one before; the «când» lines on `/admin/emails` say the same.

**Decided without the owner (YOLO), to be corrected if wrong.** (1) The email lists texts by name, not by «§»: the platform keeps no per-text change log, only «newer than the text in force», and a decision number means nothing to the club's Administrators. (2) It lists every text whose template is newer, not only those new since the last email, because the button regenerates all of them and the Administrator should see everything still owed; the trigger is still only an unannounced change. (3) The hour is 08:00 club time for both environments; QA announces to QA's Administrators on the same rule.

**Refused.** A new table or column for the mark (the row had it). A weekly digest (the owner's «prea des» is about the same-night repeats, and a day is the grain the club approves in). A separate scheduled job (a step of the maintenance job, as §639).
changelogLine: - **The «Șabloanele textelor legale s-au schimbat» email is a daily digest** — at most one a day, from 08:00 Romanian time, naming every template that changed, with the sentence that one sitting approves them all; six releases in a night no longer mean six emails. Amends §639. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Given templates that change several times between two mornings, when the maintenance job runs, then at most one `LEGAL_TEMPLATES_CHANGED` email per person goes per club day (Europe/Bucharest): the first run at or after 08:00 club time — 05:00Z in summer time, 06:00Z in winter time, on the wall clock — that finds a template newer than the text in force and not yet announced sends one email naming every newer text and saying one sitting approves them all; nothing goes before 08:00 or when nothing changed, and a change that lands after the day's email is in the next day's (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given the digest of the legal templates' changes, then its mark («the last digest», `announcedAt`) is kept in the `platform_settings` row `legalTemplatesNotice` and written with the emails, so a restart reads it back and sends nothing a second time the same day; the recipients, the per-person-per-change idempotency key and `/admin/tasks`' per-text rows are unchanged, and the email's words, in both languages, say that it comes at most once a day (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
